summary_md: **Artificial Intelligence Papers ([@SciFi](https://x.com/SciFi/status/2116557769763348642))** shares *Agent-Conditioned Routing* by Kalyanasundaram et al. ([arXiv 2610.37375](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37375)), which gets diverse reasoning paths from one frozen MoE model by giving parallel trajectories persistent expert-eligibility masks, with no fine-tuning or role prompts.

referenced_urls.title: Agent-Conditioned Routing: Diverse Reasoning Paths Within One Frozen Model

relevance: Diversity from MoE routing in one model.

media.description: Abstract of the Agent-Conditioned Routing (ACR) paper on diverse reasoning paths from one frozen sparse MoE.
media.ocr_text: Generating several solutions can expose alternative methods, but additional trajectories often paraphrase one dominant approach. We investigate whether the conditional capacity of a frozen sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) model can provide such diversity from one problem prompt, without user-assigned roles, prescribed methods, fine-tuning, or model copies. Agent-Conditioned Routing (ACR) assigns $m$ parallel trajectories persistent, untrained shared/private expert-eligibility masks while preserving the learned, input-dependent token router. On a screened 126-question multi-mode mathematics and physics benchmark, with model judges reading the reported derivations in full, we count the number of problems yielding at least two distinct primary methods among soft-correct solutions in four trajectories.
